analysis.title: Monthly Economic Update October 2026: Same fears, different crisis
key_insights: ING argues France is not Greece 2010: the primary deficit is close to 3% of GDP and the debt ratio is similar to Italy in 2011 and Greece in 2009, but France's current account is roughly balanced, household savings rate is about 18%, and the effective rate on its debt stock is below nominal GDP growth. ING says France has a fiscal problem, not a funding problem, and fears of a new euro crisis are overdone.

Oil: ING keeps its 4Q26 Brent forecast at $80/bbl and FY27 at $71/bbl, but calls 4Q26 a low-conviction call. Persian Gulf flows are back to 70-75% of pre-war levels, yet a large risk premium remains without a US-Iran deal. Tanker freight rates are at record levels and diesel remains tight.

European gas: TTF is at its highest since December 2022 and Persian Gulf LNG flows are down about 80% YoY. Storage is a little under 75% full versus a five-year average of 89%. ING raised its 26/27 winter TTF forecast to EUR73/MWh from EUR65/MWh and expects a sharp sell-off from 2Q27.

Fed: ING expects a 25bp hike in December, no October move, and no further hikes in 2027 even though markets price a further 50bp. ING does not rule out an additional hike in 1Q27 if the Iran conflict lasts. Housing is weak, with mortgage rates above 7.5%.

ECB: ING expects one more hike in December taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, not necessarily in October. The rise in German bond yields since September has had roughly the effect of a 25bp hike, and for France closer to 50bp. ING expects the ECB to halt QT before year-end.

ECB and France: ING sees the bar for activating TPI as high because it requires compliance with the EU fiscal framework, at minimum full adoption of the French budget. Expected defence is dovish rate policy first, then a flexible pause of QT reinvestment, with TPI as the last resort.

Bank of England: ING now expects two hikes, in November and February, as an insurance move, with UK CPI briefly above 4% in early 2027 on a roughly 20% January rise in household energy bills. ING still sees rate cuts possible by late 2027, while markets price about 100bp of hikes over the next year.

Bank of Japan: market prices very low odds of a hike on 30 October after the 25bp hike to 1.25% last month. ING sees the next hike in December or January, with a slight preference for January and April, and a terminal rate in the 1.75-2.00% area next year.

US rates: ING's Padhraic Garvey sees at least one more leg of long-end weakness, with the US 10-year yield returning to the 5.25%-5.5% range and possibly staying elevated into 1Q27. ING sees about 4.75% by 2027 on 2% growth and 2% inflation.

FX: ING sees EUR/USD in a 1.10-1.15 range for the next three to six months, with real rate differentials at 2022 wides. Hawkish Fed pricing and French fiscal concerns drive this. A key risk to the dollar is a renewed rise in foreign investor FX hedge ratios after White House intervention.

US midterms on 3 November: Democrats lead polls by about eight points. ING lays out three scenarios: Republican hold sends the 10-year above 5.5% and the 2-year to around 5% with the dollar strongest; Democrats take the House only is the base case and mostly priced in; a Democratic clean sweep is a mild dollar negative with a 10-year toward 5.5% without breaking above. A debt ceiling issue could arrive by mid-summer 2027, risking a prolonged shutdown.

France's 2027 budget targets a 5% deficit (from 5.4% in 2026) with €43bn of measures, versus about 6.5% without them. ING expects adoption via Article 49.3 and expects the government to survive, but even full adoption would not stabilise debt. Debt is 119% of GDP in mid-2026, rising to 121.7% in 2027. ING forecasts French GDP growth of 0.3% in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027.

ING outlines three inflation scenarios: base case with Q4 Brent at $80/bbl, an 'inflation bliss' case with $75/bbl, and a 'persistent inflation' case with $115/bbl in Q4 and $130 in Q1 and inflation hitting 5% in early 2027, in which hikes exceed market pricing and EUR/USD falls to 1.05-1.10.

Eurozone: HICP rose to 3.8% in September with underlying at 2.5%. ING expects headline above 4% by year-end, 2026 GDP growth of 1.0% and 2027 of 1.2%, with second-round effects more muted than in 2022-23.

China: after the 28 September State Council meeting, the PBOC cut the one-year pledged supplementary lending rate by 25bp to 1.5% and Beijing announced a first-ever nationwide mortgage interest subsidy for first-time buyers. The US-China trade truce was extended to January 2027. ING expects 2026 CPI of 0.9% and further stimulus if momentum stays weak.

Asia: AI-linked export growth is showing early signs of cooling, and ING expects rate hikes in all Asian economies it covers except China. ING is bearish on the Indian rupee, Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah and mildly bullish on the Korean won, Singapore dollar and Taiwan dollar.

CEE and CIS: ING expects two 25bp NBP hikes in 1Q27 to 4.25%, the CNB turning more hawkish, a 25bp Hungarian cut in December, and EUR/HUF toward 350-355 if Hungary delivers fiscal consolidation. Kazakhstan's tenge is up 11% since the Iran war began.

US economy is diverging: high-income spending and tech capex drive growth while middle and lower incomes are squeezed, with 8.6% of households spending more than 40% of income on debt obligations. Manufacturing has added 72,000 jobs year to date.

sector_views.rationale: Oil expected to fall into year-end to $80/bbl Brent in 4Q26 but low conviction. European gas is the bigger near-term risk, with TTF at €75/MWh in 4Q26.

risk_factors: Escalation of the Middle East conflict pushing Brent toward $115/bbl in 4Q and $130 in 1Q in the persistent inflation scenario.
French fiscal and political deadlock, including a budget failing by 17 December or a no-confidence vote, with spillover to other indebted eurozone sovereigns.
Further long-end bond sell-off, with a path to 5.5-6% on the US 10-year if a macro boom or persistently high inflation arrives or the US fiscal story unravels.
Winter gas supply shortfall given low EU storage and absent Persian Gulf LNG, with El Niño-driven mild weather a partial offset.
US government shutdown and debt ceiling issue by mid-summer 2027 after the midterms.
Renewed White House intervention in financial, trade or foreign policy raising foreign investor FX hedge ratios and weighing on the dollar.
AI investment bottlenecks lifting power prices and core goods inflation, and a cooling of AI-related exports in Asia.
vol_and_positioning: French 10-year swap spread has doubled from the 60bp area to the 120bp area, and French spreads to Germany are as wide as at any point since the euro's start.
Italian spreads have shown low beta to the French widening, a gradual improvement since Meloni took office.

Markets price about 75bp of ECB hikes (scaled back from almost four hikes to around one), about 50bp of further Fed hikes (three hikes over 12 months per FX section), and about 100bp of BoE hikes over the next year.
Foreign investor FX hedge ratios on US assets are back at very low levels, and foreigners have kept their share of US bond and equity markets steady at about 20%.
Real rate differentials between the US and euro area are at their widest since 2022.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict is broadening, with the Houthis in Yemen increasingly targeting Saudi Arabia, and no US-Iran deal in place.
Persian Gulf oil supply has recovered to 70-75% of pre-war levels, while LNG flows remain down about 80% YoY.
US midterm elections on 3 November, with Democrats leading polls by about eight points and prediction markets anticipating a Democratic takeover of Congress.

US-China trade truce extended to January 2027 after President Xi's September visit, with a possible leaders' meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November and the G20 in Florida on 14-15 December.
EU-China trade talks reached an initial agreement including fewer hybrid vehicle exports from China to the EU, while a Merz-Macron letter called for tougher trade tools.
French presidential election on 18 April and 2 May 2027, with the National Rally leading first-round polls.
Joint US-Japan intervention in the yen in July.
Ukraine and Iran war developments described as muddy, keeping rates markets on edge.

tension_points.bull_case: France is not Greece: current account roughly balanced, household savings rate about 18%, effective interest rate on the debt stock below nominal GDP growth, and a eurozone firewall that did not exist 16 years ago. ING sees a fiscal problem, not a funding problem.
tension_points.bear_case: Debt ratio similar to Italy in 2011, primary deficit close to 3% of GDP, a long record of missing targets, a fragmented parliament and a presidential election in 2027. Even full adoption of the budget would not stabilise debt, and the firewall was built for smaller countries.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to adopt the budget by the 17 December deadline, or a deadlock lasting until summer, would sharply worsen public finances; a further deterioration could force the ECB to prove whether its 'whatever it takes' commitment holds.

tension_points.bull_case: Persian Gulf flows are recovering toward 70-75% of pre-war levels, and with continued supply or a US-Iran deal the risk premium should erode, pulling Brent to $80/bbl in 4Q26.
tension_points.bear_case: The conflict is broadening, the market still prices a large risk premium, tanker freight rates are at records, and diesel remains tight.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Absence of a US-Iran deal, or a deepening of the crisis through winter, which would be the persistent inflation scenario with Brent at $115/bbl in Q4.

tension_points.bull_case: ING expects only one more hike in December and none in 2027 as inflation fades once Strait of Hormuz flows normalise and housing and wage pressures cool.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price a further 50bp of hikes, and a prolonged conflict could mean an additional hike in 1Q27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A longer-lasting US-Iran conflict rather than an agreement to restore Persian Gulf energy flows.
